title: Add timeout and retry to the exchange rate call
summary: An Http call that hangs for the default 30 seconds and ignores a 500 gets timeout, retry and throw.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Services;

use Illuminate\Http\Client\ConnectionException;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http;

class ExchangeRateClient
{
    public function rates(string $base): array
    {
        try {
            $response = Http::get('https://api.example.com/v1/rates', ['base' => $base]);
        } catch (ConnectionException $e) {
            return [];
        }

        return $response->json('rates');
    }
}

turns.user: when the rates api is down the dashboard hangs ~30s then dies with a TypeError. add timeout + retry. if it's down just return an empty array, the view deals with it

assistant.body: Great catch! Two things are going on. The Http facade waits 30 seconds by default. And a 500 is not an exception, so json('rates') comes back null and the array return type rejects it.

Here's the fix. timeout cuts the wait to 3 seconds, retry makes 3 attempts with 1 second in between, and throw turns a failed response into a RequestException. That and a connection error are both caught, so the caller always gets an array.

turns.user: logs show all 3 attempts in the same second. that's not 1 second apart

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. The second argument to retry is in milliseconds, unlike timeout, which counts seconds. I wrote 1, so it waited 1 millisecond.

turns.user: also it hits a 404 three times? a 404 won't fix itself, just give up

assistant.body: Right. retry takes a third argument, a callback that decides whether to try again. It receives a ConnectionException when there was no connection, or a RequestException when the response failed. So retry the first kind and any 5xx, and throw a 4xx straight away. The existing catch still picks it up, so the result is the same empty array.
